Hello,

I am following up regarding my pending Form I-129F petition, which has been
pending since April 2025. It is now October 2026, meaning the petition has
been pending for approximately 18 months without a decision or substantive
update.

As we discussed before, the prolonged delay is especially difficult for my
family. I have a 10-month-old son who is a U.S. citizen, and our continued
separation is causing significant emotional and practical hardship. Each
additional month prolongs our separation and prevents us from moving
forward together as a family.

USCIS previously advised that I should expect a decision or further action
within 60 days. That period has passed without a decision or substantive
update. Your office subsequently submitted a congressional inquiry on my
behalf, and more than 30 days have now passed since that inquiry without a
substantive response or action from USCIS.

Please if you will, contact the USCIS congressional liaison directly to
request an explanation for the continued delay and a detailed status
update. I would appreciate confirmation that the inquiry has been escalated
through the appropriate congressional liaison channel rather than submitted
as another general case-status request.

Specifically, please ask USCIS to confirm:

   1. Whether the petition is currently assigned to an adjudicating officer;
   2. Whether USCIS is waiting for any additional information or
   documentation from me or the beneficiary;
   3. Whether any additional review, background check, or other hold is
   delaying adjudication; and
   4. When USCIS expects to take action on the petition.

Please let me know when your office has contacted the USCIS congressional
liaison and provide any substantive response , I apologize if I sound a bit
desperate, it’s just incredibly difficult having life on hold and missing
so much. I have no idea what else I can do in this situation.

Thank you for your continued assistance.

James Weeks

messages.subject: Urgent Help Needed – Second USCIS RFE – WAC2590104055 james weeks
messages.body:
Hello Nathan,

I'm reaching out again because I've received another Request for
Evidence from USCIS, and I'm honestly getting pretty overwhelmed with
this process.

This latest RFE seems considerably more complicated than the last one,
and the deadline is November 16. They're asking for court dispositions
again, along with police reports, additional details about old cases,
and certified statements from the courts explaining why certain
records are unavailable.

The problem is that I already traveled back to Massachusetts and
obtained what I was told were the complete records available from the
courts. Some of these cases are nearly 20 years old, and the courts
simply don't have all the detailed documentation USCIS is now
requesting. I can't realistically travel back to Massachusetts and go
through that entire process again, especially with such a short
deadline.

I'm really hoping your office still has copies of everything I
previously sent, particularly all the court dispositions. If you could
please send me copies of those documents, along with whatever was
submitted in response to the first RFE, I can compare them against
this new request and figure out exactly what's missing.

I'm also hoping you can advise me on how we're supposed to respond
when the courts no longer have the records USCIS is requesting.
They're asking for certified statements confirming that records are
unavailable, and I don't know how I'm supposed to obtain all of that
in the time they've given me, particularly from overseas.

I'm beginning to feel like no matter what documentation I provide,
USCIS is going to keep finding something else to ask for. It's
frustrating and, frankly, discouraging. We've already been waiting so
long, and I'm worried that this is eventually going to end in a denial
despite my efforts to comply.

I know your office is busy, and I appreciate the help you've provided
so far, but I really need some guidance on this as soon as possible.
Even just getting copies of my previous submissions would give me
somewhere to start.

I don't want to lose this petition over documents that may no longer exist.

Thank you for your time and help.

James Weeks

messages.subject: Urgent certified custody records and case identification — James Michael Weeks — December 29, 2015
messages.body:
Dear Records Access Officer,

I am out of state and need these records delivered by email or secure
download. I cannot appear at your office or arrange in-person
collection. USCIS issued a Request for Evidence dated October 14,
2026, for my Form I-129F petition and must receive my complete
response by November 16, 2026. I respectfully request expedited
electronic access to my own records.I will pay any fees associated
with that.

My name is James Michael Weeks jr. Please also search the name James
Michael Weeks. and the case-name format Weeks, JR, James Michael, as
used in the USCIS notice. Date of birth: April 7, 1986 (as shown in my
supplied CORI).

The notice identifies “12/29/2015, PLYMOUTH COUNTY SD JAIL HOC,
PLYMOUTH, MA” and the label “OTHER FELONY-CRIMINAL HARRASSMENT.” It
also identifies Brockton PD and docket 1515CR005525 with a date of
10/30/2000. I cannot tell from the notice whether these refer to the
same underlying matter. Please establish any connection from your
records. My supplied January 2, 2025 CORI lists 1515CR005525A at
Brockton District Court, Brockton Police, court appearance 12/29/2015,
and labels the charge MISDEMEANOR. Please reconcile your original
booking/commitment records with these references and the RFE’s OTHER
FELONY label.

Please provide certified true copies of the booking/intake record,
charge and case-number records, commitment/mittimus and
release/discharge documents, custody dates and legal basis for
custody, and any arrest, incident or probable-cause narratives
received or generated for this matter. Please identify the committing
court, court docket, arresting/transporting agency and its report
number, and whether 12/29/2015 records a booking, transfer, arrest,
sentence, or another event.

Please provide any documents in your custody relating to a diversion
or pretrial intervention agreement, terms, conditions, completion or
termination, and final disposition for this matter. If your records
show no such program, please state what records were located and
identify the court, probation department or program custodian that
could clarify the disposition. Please include any other
custody/arrest/charge records concerning me held by your office and
identify the corresponding court and agency.

If a requested record is unavailable, please provide an original
signed or certified custodian letter specifying the record and case,
scope of search, reason for unavailability and any surviving records
or transfer destination. If it is restricted rather than missing,
please state the restriction and the subject/counsel-access route.

I am requesting access as the person who is the subject of these
records. If a public-records request is not the correct procedure,
please explain the defendant/subject-access procedure, required
authorization, or court order. If records are restricted, sealed,
impounded, or exempt, please distinguish that from records that do not
exist or cannot be located, identify the restriction in writing, and
explain how my attorney or I can seek lawful access.

Please send the records as PDF attachments to jamesmweeksjr@gmail.com,
or provide a secure download link I can access from out of state.
Include every page, certification page, signature and seal.

Please provide electronically certified PDFs if your office offers
them, or complete scans of the certified records already issued or
retained in your file.

If only uncertified scans are available electronically, please send
them promptly and clearly identify their certification status so my
attorney can address the USCIS requirement.

Please explain any electronic-access or certification restriction in
writing; inability to email a record is different from the record not
existing.

Please provide remote identification, signed-release and payment
instructions, your request reference, and expected completion date.

My requested target is November 2, 2026, for attorney review before
USCIS’s November 16 receipt deadline. I need electronic delivery only
and cannot attend or arrange pickup in Massachusetts.

Thank you,
James Michael Weeks
Email: jamesmweeksjr@gmail.com
Telephone: 13072122648
Records delivery: email or secure download
